title: I Took the Community-Kayak Checkout to the Lead Who Skipped the Hull Log

parts.text: I stepped into rack C at 8:04 a.m. and lead Soren was already using my numbered kayak. The board said: ONE HULL. NINETY MINUTES. LOG EVERY SCRATCH. I was thirty, paddle steward, holding a clipboard that listed our launch. Soren shrugged. "Leads skip the ink." I photographed the board, the booking, and his paddle in my cockpit. Then I asked for the hull log. At 8:12 the harbor desk pinged why Soren launched without a scratch line. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The harbor desk can see Soren in cockpit C during our launch.

social.video_title: He skipped the hull log on my numbered kayak — Part 1/2
social.description: Community kayak, a lead in my cockpit, a ninety-minute clock he posted. I logged the launch. Would you have asked for the hull log?

parts.text: Soren called it tide windows until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the cockpit still. The kayak went back to my numbered rack. Soren ran a slot of their own and told the next lead atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: LEADS DO NOT SKIP THE INK. I keep our launch on a labeled slate. Soren brown-bags his tides. The rack finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Leads do not skip the ink — Part 2/2
social.description: Hull log, numbered kayak, and a second line on the board. Was a tide window ever our launch?
